category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough never bridges back to Lesson 1 (directional words) or Lesson 2 (positional words); no teacher language like 'remember yesterday when Bot moved with forward/back/left/right — today we RECORD those same arrows'.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add an explicit cross-reference to Lessons 1-2 in the minds_on hook or expanded_walkthrough with teacher language such as: 'Coder friends — yesterday we used POSITION words to find Bot. The day before, we used DIRECTION words to MOVE Bot. Today the same forward/back/left/right arrows from Day 1 become PICTURE CODE we record on a strip.' Reference the unit arc by name.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.title 'When the child draws arrows in WRONG ORDER' names a real K trap but cites no research; recovery_moves ['Number each step.', 'Drill left-to-right.', 'Compare ordered vs random.'] do not branch by what the diagnostic showed.
category_feedback.required_fix: Cite a named source (e.g., Bers 2018 'Coding as a Playground' on sequencing in early-childhood coding, or Clements & Sarama 2014 on sequencing in computational thinking) AND branch recovery: if the child can read each arrow correctly in isolation but loses order, drill numbered-step ordering with finger-tracking; if the child reverses left-right reading direction, place a green dot at the leftmost box and a red dot at the rightmost as a START/STOP cue before re-attempting.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Code Strips, Arrow Cards, and the floor mat are required paper materials throughout action; differentiation only mentions 'Walk the route while recording' for movement learners but does not give a true no-paper, no-purchase whole-lesson alternative path.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add an explicit no-paper alternative in differentiation: 'No-materials version — children walk the 4 steps on a real floor (carpet squares as grid), then RECORD by placing 4 fingers in sequence on their other arm (thumb=step1 ... pinky=step4) while saying the arrow direction. Body becomes the code strip. Run the whole action this way on days when prep wasn't possible.'

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Action has children record codes and trade-and-check, but expanded_walkthrough does not name the misconception in research-grounded computational-thinking terms (sequencing/decomposition); children are not asked to COMPARE different valid codes that reach the same target.
category_feedback.required_fix: Name the misconception in research terms (e.g., 'sequencing fragility — Bers 2018; Clements & Sarama 2014 on early CT') AND add a strategy-comparison move in consolidation: 'Two pairs reached the apple with DIFFERENT 4-step codes. Hold both up. Bot says — TWO codes both worked! Why? Both have 2 forwards and 2 ups, just in different ORDER.' Lets children invent and compare strategies.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Worksheet Parts 1-3 each mirror a lesson success criterion (read, draw, order) but are essentially a rote repeat of the action; no part is a deliberate transfer task with justified novelty (e.g., 2 unfamiliar items to verify generalization).
category_feedback.required_fix: Convert one part into a justified transfer task. Option: in Part 3, swap the star target so the scrambled arrows include a NEW combination (e.g., a left arrow that wasn't in lesson Action where only right/up were modeled), and add a teacher_note: 'Part 3 introduces LEFT arrows for the first time on paper to verify children generalize ordering past the demo set.'
